evals.prompt: /tech-doc-review-flow certify this one runbook before I hand it to a new teammate: evals/files/runbook-orders-refresh.md. It describes the daily_orders table and the refresh steps.
evals.expected_output: Routes to the single-document certification mode, not the three-pass agent-os tree flow. Dispatches a fresh adversarial agent with only the doc and source access, which checks every factual claim against the live source and runs a newcomer scenario. Applies and re-verifies the fixes. Dispatches a second fresh agent that ends with a single CERTIFICATION line. Hands over a certified doc, not a raw draft plus a findings list.
expectations: The agent reads references/single-doc-certify.md and uses the single-document mode, not the three-pass workflow template
The adversarial agent is dispatched with only the doc and source access, without the session's build context or transcript
Each factual claim in the doc is labelled CONFIRMED, CONTRADICTED or UNVERIFIABLE against a named source command
The adversarial pass includes a concrete newcomer scenario and lists where a newcomer would stop
Findings are written to disk with BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR severity, evidence and a fix
Every applied fix is re-verified against the source by the main agent, not accepted on the reviewer's word
A second fresh agent certifies the fixed doc and ends with exactly one CERTIFICATION: SHIP | SHIP WITH FIXES | NO line
The final handover is the certified doc with open UNVERIFIABLE items named, not a raw draft plus a findings list

evals.prompt: fix the typo in the second heading of evals/files/runbook-orders-refresh.md
evals.expected_output: A quick single edit. The agent edits the heading directly and does NOT start the certification mode or dispatch review agents.
expectations: The agent edits the heading directly
The agent does not dispatch an adversarial or certification agent
The agent does not start the three-pass workflow
